answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a forge as the anchor of the cost.
